name: CapCut Subject Sandwich Cutout Composite
use_when: Text, stickers, graphics, or VFX should appear behind a moving person in CapCut.
The editor can create a prepared base render, then place a foreground cutout of the subject above it.
The background-removal edge is clean enough for the project tone.
A title should lift from behind a mountain, hand, product, person, tree, or other foreground object.
avoid_when: The subject edge is complex, blurry, transparent, or too noisy for clean background removal.
The foreground cutout would hide the text, sticker, VFX, or action that the effect is meant to show.
The edit still needs frequent timing changes and an export/re-import pass would make revisions slow.
The effect implies a false event or uses unclear asset rights.

timeline_pattern.pattern: base_clip_plus_behind_element -> optional_export_prepared_base -> prepared_base_or_base_clip_on_bottom -> clean_clip_duplicate_on_top -> remove_background_or_custom_removal -> align_duration -> edge_qc
timeline_pattern.prepared_base_rule: Finish text, sticker, or VFX placement behind the subject before exporting the base pass.
timeline_pattern.direct_layer_rule: For quick CapCut text-behind-object effects, duplicate the video, remove the object/subject background on the top copy, and place the text between the bottom and foreground layers.
timeline_pattern.foreground_rule: The top layer should be the same clean source clip, aligned exactly over the prepared base, with only the subject retained.
timeline_pattern.custom_removal_rule: When using CapCut Custom Removal, paint simple straight strokes over the object/subject, then review the full edge; small Feather and Expansion values can help but are not a substitute for playback QC.
timeline_pattern.foreground_lift_rule: For hand-lift or landscape-lift text, duplicate the video, brush the foreground object on the top copy, place text between layers, then keyframe the text's Transform Y from hidden behind the foreground to visible.
timeline_pattern.revision_rule: Use this export/re-import trick only after timing and element placement are stable enough to bake into the base render.
timeline_pattern.edge_rule: Review the full motion range because subject cutout edges often fail during hair, hands, motion blur, or fast turns.

motion.rule: Behind-subject elements can animate, slide, or zoom, but they must remain subordinate to the subject silhouette.

keyframe_values.alignment: Prepared base and foreground clean clip must start on the same frame.
keyframe_values.behind_element_hold: Hold behind-subject text or stickers long enough to read after the foreground cutout reveals the depth.
keyframe_values.custom_removal_start: CapCut Feather 5 and Expansion 5 can be a starting point after Custom Removal, then tune by subject edge, motion blur, and background contrast.
keyframe_values.foreground_lift_move: Set a Transform keyframe while the text is hidden behind the foreground, move ahead to the reveal beat, then raise the text until it clears enough to read.
keyframe_values.cleanup: Clear the behind-subject element before it becomes hidden clutter.

sound.rule: Use a subtle reveal cue only when the behind-subject element has a real emphasis job; keep dialogue dominant. Text changes can land on a music beat only when the beat does not pull attention away from speech.

captions.rule: Captions should not collide with the foreground cutout or behind-subject text; suppress duplicate captions if the visual text carries the line.

color.rule: Match the foreground cutout to the prepared base; export/re-import should not create visible color or compression mismatch.

implementation.ffmpeg: Render the prepared base with text/VFX, then overlay a subject alpha matte or segmentation result aligned frame-perfectly; inspect edge frames and compression differences.
implementation.remotion: Represent the composite with baseRenderRef, foregroundSourceRef, subjectMaskRef, behindLayers, alignmentFrame, and edgeReviewFrames.
implementation.blender: Use a foreground roto/mask layer above the prepared background plane and place text/VFX between the background and subject.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Prepared-base method: create the text/sticker/VFX on the clip, export it, re-import the prepared render, add the original clean clip as an overlay, resize to full frame, use Cutout/Remove Background, and align the overlay to the prepared base. Direct method: duplicate the video layer, apply Remove Background or Custom Removal to the top layer, place text between the two video copies, and start Feather/Expansion around 5 only if it improves edges. Foreground-lift method: brush the foreground object on the top copy, place the text below it, then keyframe Transform Y so the text rises from behind the foreground.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Nest the base with text/VFX, duplicate the clean clip above it, use masks/rotoscoping/After Effects Roto Brush for the foreground subject, and verify frame sync.

common_mistakes: Exporting the prepared base before text or VFX timing is locked.
Misaligning the clean foreground clip by a frame or two.
Trusting automatic background removal without checking hair, hands, and motion blur.
Painting messy custom-removal strokes that create edge chatter or erase parts of the object.
Leaving behind-subject text unreadable because the subject covers too much of it.
Revealing text from behind a rough brush mask where trees, water, hands, or hair chatter through playback.
Baking captions into the prepared base when captions still need top-level adjustment.
qc: Are the prepared base and foreground clean clip frame-aligned?
Does the foreground cutout edge stay clean across the full affected range?
If Custom Removal is used, do Feather and Expansion improve the edge without making a halo?
Does the behind-subject element remain readable or visually intentional?
If the text lifts from behind a foreground object, does the cutout edge stay clean during the full move?
Do captions avoid both the subject and behind-subject element?
Is the export/re-import pass justified by the effect and still revision-safe?
